subject: Renewal: EU residency + APAC rollout — failover schedule and capacity uplift
messages:
From: Emily Warren <emily.warren@medisync.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 10:12:00 -0400
Subject: Renewal: EU residency + APAC rollout coordination

Hi Vivek —

Thanks again for the renewal proposal your team sent last week. Two quick priorities from our side as we lock the 2028 contract:

1) EU residency: we need explicit wording confirming data-at-rest for EU traffic will be stored in the Frankfurt tenancy and logs retained per our audit window (7 years).
2) APAC rollout: we want a phased standby model (cold-warm-hot) for APAC with the ability to burst to hot for up to 48 hours once per quarter during peak promotions.

Procurement also flagged that the failover cadence and cutover steps must be included in the SOW — they want clear runbooks. Can you confirm whether your standard renewal amendment covers the above, or if we should expect separate SOW/ops attachments?

Attaching our internal compliance checklist for reference.

Thanks,
Emily Warren
Head of Cloud Ops, Medisync Health
Emily Warren | medisync.com

Attachment: Medisync_Compliance_Checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Emily Warren <emily.warren@medisync.com>; marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Renewal: EU residency + APAC rollout coordination

Emily —

Appreciate the clear asks. Short answers up front: yes, we can commit to EU data-at-rest in Frankfurt for EU-scoped traffic and provide the longer audit log retention; and yes, we support a staged APAC standby plan with documented burst windows.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa (CS lead) will draft a short amendment to the Renewal covering the residency clause and retention period.
- Ben (salesops) will model the quarterly 48‑hour burst uplift and propose a committed monthly seat/UCAP top-up for the term.
- Naomi (legal ops) will confirm language for the SOW runbook obligations and whether the runbook will be an appendix or a separate ops SOW.

Marissa — can you take the lead on the SOW draft? Ben/Naomi — please comment by EOD Wednesday so we can send a clean package to Medisync on Thursday.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | redwood.ai

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai; Emily Warren <emily.warren@medisync.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 11:27:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Renewal: EU residency + APAC rollout coordination

Hi all —

Draft SOW amendment attached (high level). Key highlights:
- EU residency clause: Frankfurt tenancy for EU traffic; logs retained for 7 years; SOC 2 audit evidence to be provided on annual cadence.
- APAC standby plan: three-tier model defined (cold <-> warm <-> hot); warm is defined as pre-warmed nodes with <15min spin-up, hot is fully provisioned with <5min readiness.
- Burst billing: we propose a burst credit pool billed at a 1.6x multiplier vs committed capacity for transient hot bursts beyond committed top-ups.
- Failover runbook: included as Appendix A — sequence of automated checks, manual ops list, rollback criteria.

Open items for procurement: specific SLA windows for the quarterly burst (we default to calendar-quarter requests; customer can pre-schedule one 48h window + two optional 24h windows).

Soojin — engineering feasibility notes are inline in the doc. Naomi — please flag any legal risk or negotiation points. Emily — can you confirm whether the procurement team needs a separate DocuSign for the SOW appendix or if a single consolidated amendment suffices?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Attachments: EU_Data_Governance_SOW_v3.pdf, APAC_Standby_SLA.xlsx

From: Tom Higgs <tom.higgs@procure-med.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai; Emily Warren <emily.warren@medisync.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 08:15:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Renewal: EU residency + APAC rollout coordination

Marissa / Emily,

Procurement here — quick procurement note: the internal legal team has requested two small edits before we can sign: 1) a liability cap carveout for data residency failures (limited to remediation costs up to 6 months of committed spend), and 2) an alternative rollback SLA if the hot-burst cannot be executed due to capacity constraints (they want a prioritized fallback to a compatible smaller model).

We'd prefer these to be dealt with in the amendment rather than a separate SOW if possible — keeps DocuSign simple. Also confirm whether you can provide a non-prod cutover rehearsal window prior to go-live (we want one run through).

Tom Higgs
Head of Procurement, Medisync Health
Tom Higgs | procure-med.com

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Emily Warren <emily.warren@medisync.com>; Tom Higgs <tom.higgs@procure-med.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: EU residency + APAC rollout coordination

Tom / Emily —

Thanks for the flag, Tom. Quick summary of agreement and actions:

1) Liability carveout: we can accept a limited remediation cap tied to committed spend (proposed language: remediation limited to 6 months of committed monthly spend, excluding consequential damages). Naomi will clean language and show redline in the amendment.

2) Rollback SLA: engineering confirms fallback to a compatible smaller model is feasible; we'll add prioritized fallback procedures to Appendix A and list model tiering and expected perf delta. Soojin will own the runbook update and schedule a non-prod rehearsal.

3) DocuSign: Marissa recommends a single consolidated amendment (amendment + Appendix A as attachment) so there's only one signing flow. We'll deliver an updated draft by Friday EOD for procurement review.

4) Schedule: proposed rehearsal date options: Aug 9, Aug 16, Aug 23 (you pick one). Please confirm availability and we will allocate an engineering runbook owner and a rehearsal checklist.

I'll track and coordinate the DocuSign flow once Naomi posts the redline and Ben confirms the pricing uplift for burst credits.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
